Christmas Advent · Lesson 7 · Upper-Intermediate

The Unwrapping

Every story has an ending. Or does it?

1. Listen to the final part of the story

What happened? Listen without reading the script the first time. On your second listen, open it if you need a little help.

Show listening script

Lily slowly opened her eyes, feeling a dull ache throughout her body. As she stared up at the plain white hospital ceiling, fragments of strange, scattered dreams drifted through her mind—images she couldn’t fully remember, but that left a strange feeling.

Just as she tried to sit up, a nurse stepped in, smiling. “Good morning, Lily,” she said softly. “You had a skiing accident, but you’re going to be just fine. I’m not sure what you remember, darling.”

Lily blinked, trying to process this. “A skiing accident?” she murmured, confused. “I don’t remember anything about it.”

“That’s normal, dear. A concussion can make things a bit foggy. You were also dreaming a lot while you were asleep. Quite restless, talking and moving around in your sleep,” the nurse added.

As she lay there, the boredom of the hospital setting began to settle in. She felt restless, already tired of lying still and waiting. Lily glanced over to the small calendar on the side table. It was December 1st.

Then an idea sparked. December 1st... it was the perfect day to start something new. She’d always wanted to write a story, something mysterious and exciting. And with all this free time, she thought, why not try?

A character formed in her mind. A girl like herself, someone curious and adventurous. “Clara,” she decided. “That’s what I’ll call her.”

With a small notepad by her bed, she picked up a pen and began letting her thoughts flow onto the page. She wrote:

Clara woke up on December 1st feeling excited and inspired...

Reveal the final line
Clara woke up on December 1st feeling excited and inspired...
